accepted.change: The scope sentence now reads 'Change parameter values only: do not add, remove or rewire any block, and keep every variable under its current name'. Two p2p graph checks enforce it (R6, tooling T1): same_blocks_as_start with variables 'value_only', and same_connections_as_start in 'isomorphic' mode. Both are listed in spec_properties. The old authoring note calling the sentence unobservable was replaced by authoring_notes.scope. Three restructuring mutants were added: the low-pass FIR swapped for fft_filter_xxx, an unused variable deleted, and the low-pass filter fed from the band-reject output. Each one is killed only by a graph check. Verified with the real ladder: the reviewer's cx_fft_filter_swap, cx_bp_cascade_added_block and cx_hp_dc_blocker_added fail V6 p2p with 'added {...}' details, and a renamed variable (cutoff_high -> lp_cutoff) fails. A renamed FIR block passes; the instruction allows it, and known limit (2) records it.

The two RRC band shares were replaced by a check that rrc.dat holds 'the same samples as now'. The reference is the start graph's own rrc.dat, samples 4096-8191, from two ladder runs that build.py asserts are identical. The checks are a signed zero-lag corr_ref >= 0.99999 (tooling T2) and an RMS within 1 % of the start graph's 0.4972. Exact equality was not used because FIR SIMD paths may round differently with buffer alignment. The instruction says 'Leave the noise source and the RRC filter exactly as they are: rrc.dat must keep receiving the same samples as now.' Verified: RRC roll-off 0.15 (0.99612) and 0.3 (0.99923), 88 taps (0.0102), uniform noise of equal power (-0.009), noise seed 1 (0.060) and noise pool 8192 (0.099) all fail. Noise amplitude 0.5 fails on the RMS. Mutants were added for alpha 0.3, ntaps 22*sps, amplitude 0.5 and uniform noise. The reference and all 15 variants score 1.000000.

The prose now agrees with the stated numbers: 'I worked out these numbers for unit-power noise and passbands that are perfectly flat with every band edge in the middle of its guard band: each 1 kHz slice next to a guard band must carry at least 90 % of the power it would carry then'. Verified: the reviewer's steep designs with edges at 3.55/7.45 kHz (slice 0.2567, RMS 0.403) and 3.95/7.05 kHz (RMS 0.358) still fail, now consistently with the text. Edges at 3.60/7.40, 3.65/7.35 and 3.85/7.15 kHz (Blackman, 80 Hz) pass.

This takes option (a): strict wording plus graph checks. v2 now puts the band plan as expressions inside the existing variables (cutoff_high = '4000 - 500/2', transition = '0.8*500', Kaiser beta 8) and adds no helper variables. v3 puts literal values in the four filter-taps blocks (Hann windows, per-filter widths, slightly off-centre edges) and keeps the five scalar variables, now unused. v4 is the reviewer's alt_inline_firdes_nowin: firdes taps written straight into the four FIR filters, with no window argument. Every other design the item-quality reviewer showed is registered as an alt_* variant. All 15 variants pass both graph checks and V6. The old v2 (3 variables added) and old v3 (5 variables deleted) were rebuilt as probes and fail V6 p2p.

Fixed in the tool by tooling T6 (ladder.load_task_file sets _dir); no task change was needed. Verified: './gb ladder items/tier_f/dev/gbf-dev-09/reference.grc --task items/tier_f/dev/gbf-dev-09/task.json' exits 0, with same_blocks_as_start 'same block types' and same_connections_as_start 'same connections'.

Every stated requirement maps to a check (build.py asserts it). The run sentence is stated: 266240 items per point, checked by V5 liveness. Each observation point names its file and item type (float). Known limits and the GPL attribution are in review.notes. R12: every band_fraction threshold comes from the stated flat-passband shares, not from measurements. All margins were re-measured with the corrected oracle over the reference and the 15 variants plus 6 extra valid designs. All pass. The tightest are band-pass RMS 0.3616 against the bound 0.361 for the reviewer's 3.9/7.1 kHz design (deterministic, seed-0 noise), the band-pass edge slice 0.2638 against 0.257 (edges 3.6/7.4 kHz), and the high-pass edge slice 0.0550 against 0.053 (the 'cutoff = passband edge' reading). Five observation points: re-gated on 18 Oct with the non-back-pressuring taps of tooling T7. build.py regenerates every file byte-identically; this was checked against the files left by the interrupted earlier fixer run.
